findings.title: Passkeys are no longer populated for initial username/password login
findings.body: `authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, but that helper includes `user != null`. In the normal initial login flow `context.getUser()` is null, so this block is skipped and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. Previously the code filled the WebAuthn context whenever passkeys were enabled and no user had been selected. As a result conditional passkeys/autofill are disabled on the first factor page, discoverable-key auto-login stops working, and tests that assert the `form[@id='webauth']` element on the initial page or after an invalid username will fail. The same helper is also used in the error `challenge(...)` method, so passkey data is lost on initial-login errors as well.

findings.title: Re-authentication shortcut is disabled for users without passkeys
findings.body: The shortcut is now disabled whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true, but that method only checks that passkeys are enabled for the realm and that the user is non-null; it does not check whether this user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential. Therefore a user with only a password who is re-authenticating in a realm with passkeys enabled will no longer proceed directly to the password step via `context.success()`, and will instead be shown an extra username/passkey form they cannot use. The feature should verify that the known user has a configured passkey before disabling this shortcut.
